title: Add MCP-backed agent authoring bridge
description:
Problem: MemorySmith already exposes task and page mutation tools through the local MCP runtime, but coding-agent sessions like this one cannot call those repo-local MCP tools directly. That forces manual JSON/file authoring for tasks and pages even when a safer product-native write path exists.

Desired outcome: provide a supported authoring bridge so coding agents can create/update tasks and draft page writes through MemorySmith MCP instead of manually editing storage files.

Scope:
- In scope: expose MemorySmith MCP tools to the coding-agent environment directly, or add a thin local helper that submits validated MCP `tools/call` requests to the app.
- In scope: support the highest-value authoring flows first: task create/update/status/comment and proposal-first page authoring.
- In scope: document prerequisites and validation for local authoring via the bridge.
- Out of scope: broad external network tool integration unrelated to MemorySmith local workflows.

Validation:
- End-to-end proof that a coding-agent workflow can create at least one task through the bridge without manual file editing.
- Focused docs describing how the bridge is available and what approval/policy gates apply.

Confidence target: 94%.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from self-review after confirming the repo runtime has MCP task/page mutation tools, but this coding-agent environment cannot call them directly, forcing manual task JSON authoring.
